notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix. §1985:VI.6.25.2 prints STRING, one or more groups of one or more identifier-1 or literal-1 closed by DELIMITED BY identifier-2, literal-2 or SIZE, then INTO identifier-3, then [WITH POINTER identifier-4], [ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-1], [NOT ON OVERFLOW imperative-statement-2] and [END-STRING] in that order. stringStatement keeps the order of the groups, INTO and POINTER (POINTER before INTO and a second INTO operand are parse errors) and BindString binds the groups; the later editions' omission of DELIMITED before INTO (§2023:14.9.43.3 SR9) is refused at 85 by VisitStringStatement (COBOL0900), with no DELIMITED phrase at all and with only the last one omitted. Probed at --std 85 with BY, WITH and ON omitted, figurative-constant senders and every delimiter alternative. What is NOT implemented is the printed sequence of the two phrases: the conditionalPhrases loop and Associates / MayAssociate ask only that a phrase is one the statement's formats print and is not yet written, with no edition arm, so the NOT phrase written before its positive twin compiles and runs at 85; either order is the 2002 change §2002:F.2 (item 33), which the row's change record names. Same mechanism as the UNSTRING and arithmetic rows of this slice. The witness runs two groups, POINTER and both phrases in the printed order.

next.reason: 1985: "{identifier-1|literal-1} … DELIMITED BY {identifier-2|literal-2|SIZE} … [ON OVERFLOW …] [NOT ON OVERFLOW …]"; 2023: "The DELIMITED phrase may be omitted only immediately preceding the INTO phrase. If it is omitted, DELIMITED BY SIZE is implied.". 1985 requires DELIMITED BY in every group. 2023 lets the one before INTO be omitted, implying SIZE. Its choice indicators also allow ON OVERFLOW and NOT ON OVERFLOW in either order.
